text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand, which helps developers find and fix problems faster. When you refactor, you might rename variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. Although refactoring takes time, it reduces technical debt, which builds up when code is written quickly and becomes messy. Good refactoring makes software easier to maintain and extend in the future. Remember, if the behavior of the program changes, it is not refactoring.
